summary: Tech Mahindra is an IT services company. Large businesses, especially phone and network companies, pay it to build, run and fix their software, computer systems and networks, using engineers in India and other countries.
description: Every large company runs on software and networks: customer accounts, billing, phone networks, factory machines, websites. Most do not want to build and look after all of it themselves. Tech Mahindra's engineers do that work for them, mainly from offices and development centres in India and in many other countries. Examples are building new software, moving a client's systems to the cloud (rented computers run by others), running a client's back-office tasks such as customer support, and protecting systems from attack. Industries it serves include telecommunications, which the report says is a significant share of revenue, manufacturing, banking and finance, healthcare and technology firms. It belongs to the Mahindra Group, which also owns other, separate listed companies.
money: Clients pay Tech Mahindra for people's time and for finished work. Some contracts pay a fixed price for a project, and the report says it recognises the revenue as the work progresses. Its biggest cost is its people: salaries for engineers, plus offices and travel, and fees to outside contractors. Profit is the gap between what clients pay and these costs. A bill sent to a client is not cash received: money arrives later, so the report tracks how fast clients pay.
customers: The clients are large companies and organisations around the world, such as phone and network operators, manufacturers, banks and hospitals. They pay for specific projects or ongoing running of a system. The report says the company adds new large clients and grows its biggest accounts, and that it depends heavily on telecom clients.
drivers: Mostly: how much clients are willing to spend on technology, the prices it can charge for its people's time, how many engineers it keeps busy, and how well it controls costs.

groups.title: Engineering services
groups.examples: Designing products and the software built into devices, testing, and chip-related work.
groups.explanation: A phone maker or car firm pays engineers to design and test its products. The work is project based and the client owns what is built.

groups.title: Running back-office work
groups.explanation: Tech Mahindra staff handle routine client work such as customer support or billing, often helped by automation. The client pays for the service, not for software.

groups.title: Cloud, networks and security
groups.examples: Digital core services: cloud, infrastructure, network and security.
groups.explanation: Moving a client's computer systems to rented cloud servers, running its networks and guarding them from attack.

groups.title: Business software
groups.examples: Setting up ERP (enterprise resource planning, software that runs accounts, buying and stock) and CRM (customer relationship management, software that tracks customers and sales).
groups.explanation: Companies buy these systems from software vendors. Tech Mahindra installs, adapts and looks after them for the client.

groups.title: Data, consulting and AI
groups.examples: Data work, design of customer experiences, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools.
groups.explanation: Advice and projects that help clients use their data, and AI-based tools the company builds, which it says it adds to every service.

basics.title: What does IT services mean?
basics.text: Companies pay another firm's engineers to build, run and fix their computer systems. The firm is paid for people's time or for finished projects, and does not sell a product off a shelf.

basics.title: Why are most staff in India?
basics.text: As general explanation, not from the report: engineers in India cost less than in the US or Europe, so clients pay less for the same work. The report says the company uses a globally spread delivery model with centres close to clients.

basics.title: What does a fixed-price project mean?
basics.text: The client agrees a price for a project. If the work takes longer than planned, the company bears the extra cost, so careful planning matters.

steps.title: A client signs a contract
steps.text: After a sales effort, a client signs for a project or for ongoing running of a system. The report tracks the value of new contracts won.

steps.title: Staff are assigned
steps.text: Engineers in India and abroad, and some outside contractors, work on the project.

steps.title: Work is delivered
steps.text: Software is built, systems are moved or run, or a service is operated day to day.

steps.title: The client is billed
steps.text: As general explanation, not from the report, the company bills monthly or at project stages and the client pays some weeks later.

steps.title: Profit is what is left
steps.text: Payments received less salaries, contractor fees, offices and other costs.

specifics.title: Telecom is a major industry
specifics.text: The report names telecommunications first among the industries it serves and says a significant share of revenue comes from telecom and communications. When phone companies cut technology spending, Tech Mahindra feels it first.

specifics.title: A three-year margin repair plan
specifics.text: The report describes Project Fortius, a programme to improve profit margins through pricing, productivity on fixed-price projects, lower contractor costs and efficiency. It calls the 2025-26 year the stabilisation phase of a three-year transformation.

specifics.title: Part of the Mahindra Group
specifics.text: The report says it is part of the Mahindra Group, but Mahindra's cars, tractors and finance arms are separate companies and are not part of its results.

watch: How much do clients spend with it?
Revenue depends on clients' technology budgets, which can be cut when economies weaken.
Look in the annual report for revenue growth, new contract wins and commentary on client spending, and compare with the year before.
The company has a plan to improve margins, and its success changes how much each sale earns.
Compare the operating margin over several years and read what the report says Project Fortius changed.
How dependent is it on telecom?
One industry cycle can move the whole company.
Check the industry split of revenue in the annual report and whether other industries are growing.
Can it keep and pay its engineers?
People are its main cost and asset, and leavers must be replaced and trained.
Look at staff leaving rates, staff utilisation and notes on pay costs in the annual report.
Does AI help or hurt its business?
AI tools may let clients do some work with fewer people, which changes what they pay for.
Read what the report says about AI offerings and compare project types and pricing over time.
risks: The report says the IT services industry is highly competitive, with domestic and global players and start-ups, and that this puts pressure on prices and needs constant spending on skills and tools.
The report names concentration risk: a significant share of revenue comes from telecom and communications, so a downturn in that industry would hit it hard.
The report says a significant portion of revenue comes from exports, so slower economies or trade tensions in key markets can reduce clients' technology spending.
Visa rules and old legal cases
The report says changing immigration rules can raise costs or limit staff moving between countries. It also says it is still addressing litigation that came from its acquisition of Satyam Computers.
context: The report calls 2025-26 the stabilisation phase of its three-year transformation plan, during which it expanded operating margins through Project Fortius, while continuing to invest in its strategy.
sources: NSE Indices Limited, NIFTY 50 constituent list (Tech Mahindra, symbol TECHM)

quick.title: What it does
quick.text: It builds, runs and fixes software, computer systems and networks for large companies, with engineers in India and other countries.

quick.title: Who pays
quick.text: Large companies around the world, including phone and network operators, manufacturers, banks and healthcare firms.

quick.title: How it earns
quick.text: From projects and ongoing services, paid by fixed price or for staff time.

quick.title: What it spends on
quick.text: Mostly salaries for its engineers, plus outside contractors, offices, travel and technology.

helps.title: Many services and industries
helps.text: The report lists engineering, back-office, cloud, business software, data and AI services across telecom, manufacturing, banking, healthcare and technology clients, so it is not tied to one service.

helps.title: Improving margins
helps.text: The report says its operating margin rose over the year, helped by pricing, productivity and lower contractor costs under Project Fortius.

helps.title: A spread-out delivery model
helps.text: The report describes engineers close to clients in many countries and a large offshore share, which keeps costs down while staying near customers.

hurts.title: Dependence on telecom
hurts.text: A significant share of revenue comes from telecom and communications, whose spending can swing.

hurts.title: Price pressure from rivals
hurts.text: The report says competition puts pressure on prices and forces constant investment in new skills and tools.

hurts.title: Spending tied to client budgets
hurts.text: The report says export revenue makes it sensitive to the economies of its key markets, because that affects client technology spending.
